mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital for corporations and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 0.5% in a single month, it signals the start of a monetary tightening cycle, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS) and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market that fuels consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-recession recovery phase, a sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1200 thousand units signals strong consumer confidence and construction activity, which drives corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during post-recession recovery when HOUST exceeds 1200 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0 in a month, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain disruptions, which reduces corporate output and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where INDPRO falls below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales index (RSAFS) over the past 3 months reflects strong consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS has increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% and a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals an overheating economy that prompts aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and UNRATE < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of supply chain disruption, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates worsening manufacturing conditions, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during supply chain disruption when INDPRO falls below 105.0.
